title: Magnesium

review.note: Drafted from the source below; not yet reviewed by a medical professional.

measures: A magnesium blood test measures the amount of magnesium in your blood. Magnesium is a mineral that helps muscles, nerves, and the heart work, supports bones and the immune system, and helps control blood pressure and blood sugar.
context: You get magnesium from foods such as nuts, seeds, beans, leafy greens, and milk, and the kidneys and intestines control how much stays in your blood. A result outside the normal range does not always mean a condition that needs treatment; many medicines and supplements can raise or lower it, and low levels are more common than high levels.
aboveRange: Getting too much magnesium from supplements, laxatives, antacids, or certain medicines
A problem clearing magnesium, most often from kidney failure
Other conditions such as dehydration, an underactive thyroid, an adrenal gland condition, or overactive parathyroid glands
belowRange: Not getting enough magnesium in the diet
Trouble absorbing magnesium, such as with digestive conditions or certain medicines
Losing too much magnesium, such as from kidney problems, long-term diarrhea, or diabetes
Other conditions such as underactive parathyroid glands or pregnancy
nextStep: Discuss this result with your doctor.
